subject: language_arts

unit.title: Fluent reading: longer words & expression
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I read big words and long sentences smoothly, like a storyteller?

topic: Fluency review: syllable-chopping and expressive reading
title: Fluency review: beat the robot
objectives: By the end, I can syllable-chop new words and read a passage fluently.

vocabulary.definition: reading a word instantly, no sounding out

emphasize: This is a retrieval lesson — the child does the doing. Two skills together: beat-read any long word, then read a passage like a storyteller.
Keep the 'Robot vs Storyteller' framing — robot read first, then beat it with the smooth read. You always win the second time.
Catch any return to one-gulp reading (chop it) or robotic reading (re-read for fluency) — and guessing long words from the first letter.

keyConcepts: retrieval of the two-read fluency secret (L3)
combining both skills on one passage
misconceptions: sliding back to one-gulp reading of long words
skipping the second (fluency) read and moving on
guessing long words from the first letter
hooks: Robot versus Storyteller — a face-off you always win the second time.
priorKnowledge: read once to decode, again for fluency (Lesson 3)

digital: four long-word cards on screen (picnic, elephant, stegosaurus, playground)
review passage with . ? and ! (Sam ran to the park. He saw a huge dog! Where did the dog come from? It wagged its tail. Sam laughed and clapped.)
speak blocks — the tutor listens to every read

plan.goal: Set up the Robot vs Storyteller face-off; retrieve beat-reading with playground.
plan.note: Quick demo of robot-then-storyteller on one sentence so the frame is vivid. The child always wins the second read — say so.
plan.successCriteria: Child beat-reads playground (2 beats) and is ready for the face-off.

script.say: It's a face-off: Robot versus Storyteller! Here's how it works — you read it once the robot way, all flat and bumpy… then you BEAT the robot with a smooth, lively read. You always win the second time. Ready, champion? Warm up first — read playground by its beats.
script.adaptHints: If the child liked a particular character voice from Lesson 3, promise it can appear in today's storyteller reads. If playground is shaky, clap and dot it first.

blocks.caption: Robot vs Storyteller — you win the second read!

blocks.prompt: Warm-up — read this by its beats.

stuckProtocol: If playground is shaky: clap it, dot the two beats, read each, blend — the Lesson 1 routine.

plan.goal: Quick refresh of both tricks: chop the big words; re-read for the smooth win.
plan.note: Short and brisk — this is retrieval, not new teaching. Model dotting stegosaurus and a robot-then-storyteller read of one sentence.
plan.successCriteria: Child can name both tricks before practising them.

script.say: Two tricks we're using today. Trick one — long words: clap or dot the beats, read each, push together. Watch — ste (dot) go (dot) sau (dot) rus (dot)… stegosaurus! Trick two — smooth reading: read once to crack the words, then read AGAIN like a storyteller, watching the punctuation. That second read is how you beat the robot. Chop the big words; re-read for the smooth win!
script.adaptHints: Keep the modelling snappy — under a minute each — so most of the lesson is the child reading.

blocks.title: The two winning moves
steps: Long words: clap or dot the beats → read each → push together
Smooth reading: read once to crack it → read again like a storyteller
Let the punctuation boss your voice: . breath · ? up · ! excitement

blocks.markdown:
**Today's passage:**

Sam ran to the park. He saw a huge dog! Where did the dog come from? It wagged its tail. Sam laughed and clapped.

plan.goal: Warm up together: beat-read elephant, then robot-and-storyteller read of the passage's first sentence.
plan.note: The child does the reading with light tutor support — this is the last scaffolded moment before independent work.
plan.successCriteria: Child beat-reads elephant and reads the first sentence twice, smoother the second time.

script.say: Let's warm up together. Beat-read this card with me — elephant… el (clap) e (clap) phant (clap)… elephant! Now one sentence of our passage. Robot read first — Sam. Ran. To. The. Park. Beep boop. Now beat the robot — your storyteller read. Go!
script.adaptHints: Laugh WITH the robot voice, then cheer the storyteller version. Quick question after: 'what should your voice do at the exclamation mark later?' — listen for: get excited.

blocks.prompt: Beat the robot! Read the first sentence smooth and lively.

check.question: On our storyteller read, what should your voice do at the exclamation mark — He saw a huge dog!

wrongAnswers.remedy: The climb is for the question mark. The exclamation is the firework — say 'He saw a huge dog!' like it's amazing news.
The mark is there to boss your voice! Imagine a HUGE dog appearing right now — tell me about it.

plan.goal: Retrieval check: read playground and name its beats.
plan.note: Same check as the outline's end-of-unit standard. Probe: 'How did you split it into two beats?'
plan.successCriteria: Child reads playground and says play-ground, 2 beats.

script.say: Quick check before the big round. Read playground — and tell me its beats.
script.adaptHints: After success, probe: 'How did you split it into two beats?'

blocks.prompt: Now read it — beats first, then the whole word.

check.question: Read playground and tell me its beats.

wrongAnswers.answer: tries to read it whole and stalls
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first — clap play-ground, then read each beat.
Hand under chin — feel the jaw drop twice — play… ground.

plan.goal: Independent round: beat-read the four word cards, then read the passage twice — decode read, then fluency read with expression.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2, biased to speak items. This is the End-of-Unit 1 evidence round. Watch for: skipping the second read, guessing long words from the first letter, ignoring ? and !.
plan.successCriteria: Child beat-reads picnic, elephant, stegosaurus, playground and reads the passage smoothly on the second pass.

script.say: The big round! First, knock down the four word cards — clap or dot, read the beats, push together. Then the passage: one robot read to crack it… then DESTROY that robot with your smoothest, liveliest storyteller read. Optional turbo: we can time your storyteller read and you can try to beat your own smoothness next time!
script.adaptHints: Offer the timer only if the child enjoys a race — smoothness beats speed, say so. Let them do a character voice on the final read if they loved that in Lesson 3.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'long word — let's chop it' or 'still bumpy — let's re-read'.
Step down: dot the beats / choose the shortest sentence.
ONE hint: read the first beat, or model the sentence to echo.
Re-ask the smaller version, then build back up.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise. One beat / one more read.'

plan.goal: Child teaches back both winning moves; end-of-unit praise on an earned win.
plan.note: This recap doubles as the End-of-Unit 1 check wrap-up. Mastery = long words read by beats; passage smooth, not word-by-word.
plan.successCriteria: Child states: chop into beats; read once to crack it, then again for fluency.

script.say: You beat the robot! Teach me both winning moves — one for long words, one for smooth reading… Yes! Chop the big words into beats, and read once to crack it, then again like a storyteller. You chopped every long word and you re-read for the smooth win — your storyteller read beat the robot every single time.
script.adaptHints: Name the exact words conquered today. Process praise only — effort and strategy, never 'clever'.

block.prompt: Card one — clap the beats, read each, push together.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: pic-nic read beat by beat, then blended: 'picnic'

wrongAnswers.why: guessing from the first letter instead of reading each beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Cover the second beat. Read just 'pic'… now 'nic'. Push them together — no guessing needed.
Clap it into beats first: pic (clap) nic (clap). One beat at a time.

hints: Two claps hide in this word.

reteach.say: Remember our Lesson 1 friend? Pic (clap), nic (clap) — two beats. Read each: pic… nic. Push: picnic! Words you've chopped before fall even faster the second time.

practiceBank.skill: re-read a short sentence for smoothness

block.prompt: Robot read once… then beat the robot with a smooth read.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Second read smooth and connected — 'The dog is big.' like talking

wrongAnswers.remedy: That was the robot's turn — now yours! Same sentence, smooth, like you're telling me about a real dog.

wrongAnswers.answer: still choppy on the second read
wrongAnswers.remedy: Crack any bumpy word first — then the storyteller read. One more time, nice and easy.

hints: First read cracks it, second read wins.
Tell it to me like news, not like a list.

reteach.say: Listen to the face-off. Robot: The. Dog. Is. Big. Storyteller: The dog is big! Same words — the second one sounds like a person. The trick is always the re-read. Your turn: robot first, then beat it.

block.prompt: Card two — clap the beats, read each, push together.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: el-e-phant read beat by beat, then blended: 'elephant'

wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under the chin: el… e… phant — three jaw drops. The little 'e' is a whole beat.
Clap it into beats first: el (clap) e (clap) phant (clap).

hints: Three beats — one of them is tiny.
el… e… phant — read each stepping stone.

reteach.say: Elephant has a tiny middle beat that loves to hide. Clap it slowly: el (clap) e (clap) phant (clap). Read all three: el… e… phant… elephant! Tiny beats count too.

block.prompt: Card three — the dinosaur! Dot the beats, read each, push together.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: ste-go-sau-rus read beat by beat, then blended: 'stegosaurus'

wrongAnswers.answer: one long blur that stops halfway
wrongAnswers.remedy: Dot it first: ste (dot) go (dot) sau (dot) rus (dot). Read one stepping stone at a time.

wrongAnswers.why: lost the thread over four beats
wrongAnswers.remedy: Join the halves: ste-go… sau-rus… now push the halves together.

hints: Four dots — place them before you read.
Halves trick: ste-go, then sau-rus, then join.

reteach.say: The dinosaur from Lesson 2 is back — and you already beat it once! Four stepping stones: ste… go… sau… rus. Join two at a time: ste-go… sau-rus… stegosaurus! Once chopped, never scary again.

practiceBank.skill: read a question with a rising voice

block.prompt: The wondering sentence — let your voice climb at the end.
block.target: Where did the dog come from?

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Read smoothly with the voice rising at the end, like real asking

wrongAnswers.remedy: Ask me for real — a mystery dog just appeared! 'Where did the dog come from?' Hear the climb on 'from'?

wrongAnswers.why: confused the question lift with exclamation excitement
wrongAnswers.remedy: That's your firework voice — save it for the huge dog sentence! Questions wonder — let the end float up gently.

hints: Pretend a mystery dog just trotted up to you.
The climb lands on the last word: from?

reteach.say: Question marks make voices climb — it's automatic when you really wonder. Try wondering for real: a strange dog appears at your door… 'Where did the dog come from?' Feel your voice float up? Now read it exactly like that.

block.prompt: Clap each word out loud, then sort it by its beats.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under the chin: el… e… phant. Count the drops — the little 'e' is a whole beat.

wrongAnswers.why: rushed the claps on a long word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Slow right down: cat… er… pil… lar. Clap each one — how many claps?

hints: Say each word OUT LOUD — beats hide in silent reading.
Longest word, most beats — but check by clapping, not by looks.

reteach.say: Sorting beats is just clapping with tidy hands! Picnic: pic-nic, two. Playground: play-ground, two. Elephant: el-e-phant, three. Dinosaur: di-no-saur, three. Caterpillar: cat-er-pil-lar — four! Clap first, sort second, every time.

block.prompt: Stretch card! Four beats, no dots given — mark them yourself, then read it.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: cat-er-pil-lar read beat by beat, then blended: 'caterpillar'

wrongAnswers.remedy: 'Cat' is stone one of four. Read the next beat on its own — no guessing, every beat gets read.
Count your stones — four dots, four beats. Read them again slowly and let all four into the word.

hints: Say it slowly and feel the jaw drops — four of them.
Join halves: cat-er… pil-lar… then push.

reteach.say: Our longest word — but you've beaten four-beat words before! Dot it: cat (dot) er (dot) pil (dot) lar (dot). Read: cat… er… pil… lar. Halves: cat-er… pil-lar… caterpillar! Four beats, all crossed.

practiceBank.skill: read a full passage fluently with expression

block.prompt: The grand final! Crack-read done? Now the full storyteller read — smooth, with every mark obeyed.
block.target: Sam ran to the park. He saw a huge dog! Where did the dog come from? It wagged its tail. Sam laughed and clapped.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Whole passage read smoothly — breath at full stops, excitement at 'a huge dog!', voice climbing at the question

wrongAnswers.answer: smooth but flat — the ! and ? sound like full stops
wrongAnswers.remedy: Beautifully smooth! Now the feelings: find the firework sentence and the wondering sentence, and let them shine on one more read.
The robot got you this time! Crack-read it once more, no rush… then take your storyteller revenge.

hints: Crack it first — the storyteller read only works on cracked words.
The firework: 'He saw a huge dog!' The wonder: 'Where did the dog come from?'

reteach.say: Let's build the show sentence by sentence. 'Sam ran to the park.' — calm. 'He saw a huge dog!' — firework! 'Where did the dog come from?' — wondering, voice climbs. 'It wagged its tail.' — warm and calm. 'Sam laughed and clapped.' — happy ending. Now join the whole show together and beat that robot.

interestSlots: let the child perform it in their favourite character voice

block.prompt: The robot wants to learn! Teach it: what are the TWO winning moves that beat it today?
block.sample: One — chop long words into beats and read each beat. Two — read once to crack the words, then read again smoothly with expression.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Chop long words into beats; read once to crack it, then re-read smoothly with expression

wrongAnswers.why: outcome named, not the strategy — and speed confused with smoothness
wrongAnswers.remedy: The robot needs the actual moves! What do you do to a LONG word before reading it? And how many times do you read a tricky sentence?
That's move one — brilliant. There were TWO today: one for big words, one for whole sentences. What was the other?

hints: One move is for long words, one is for sentences.
Think: claps and dots… then think: how many reads?

reteach.say: Here's the whole toolkit in one breath. Big word? Chop it — clap or dot the beats, read each, push together. Bumpy sentence? Re-read it — once to crack, once like a storyteller, letting the marks boss your voice. Two moves — and they beat the robot every time.

block.title: The robot-beating toolkit
steps: Long word → chop into beats → read each → push together
Marks boss the voice: . breath · ? up · ! firework

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level. At level 3, interleave the long-word speak items with the full-passage read. Prefer speak items — this review IS the child reading aloud.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach, then drop one level (shorter word / shorter sentence) for a guaranteed win.
adaptivity.masterySignal: End-of-Unit 1 standard: child beat-reads three unfamiliar long words (e.g. picnic, elephant, stegosaurus) AND reads the passage smoothly with some expression, not word-by-word → mastery ≥ 0.8 for Unit 1 fluency.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'long word — let's chop it' or 'still bumpy — let's re-read'.
Step down: dot the beats / choose the shortest sentence.
ONE hint: read the first beat, or model the sentence to echo.
Re-ask the smaller version, then build back up.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise. One beat / one more read.'
adaptivity.personalization: Offer the optional timer only if the child likes a race (smoothness beats speed). Let them perform the final passage in a favourite character voice. Never change the target words or passage.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on the child's best storyteller read and praise the process: 'you chopped every long word and re-read for the smooth win — the robot never stood a chance.'

differentiation.support: Fewer words (two cards), a shorter 2–3 sentence passage; the tutor does the decode read with the child first.
differentiation.stretch: Time the second (fluency) read and aim to beat it for smoothness; add the 4-beat caterpillar.

extension: Record a storyteller read of the passage and listen back, naming one thing done well.
assessmentEvidence: End-of-Unit 1 evidence: child beat-reads three unfamiliar long words and reads a short passage on a fluency pass with some expression — smooth, not word-by-word.
revisitLater: Bring beat-reading back as a warm-up in Unit 2 (Lesson 5 onwards); re-run the Robot vs Storyteller face-off on a fresh passage in a few weeks.
